messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: URGENT: Autoscaler health degraded for gpu-serving-cluster (prod). Queue length spike detected: ~12,400 pending requests, avg wait ~48s. Pager: @maya (oncall-ml).

maya: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Seeing huge queue growth on infer-rt; pods healthy but scale-up attempts failing with cloud API 429s.

alex: Confirmed — autoscaler tried to request new instances at 02:09:54 but cloud returned RateLimitExceeded, autoscaler backoff triggered. Metrics: scale attempts 27 in 5m, 429 rate 73%.

jess: Adding context — we've got mixed GPU families. Some model shards only fit on A100-like nodes; fallback variants exist but need routing changes. Suggest two parallel mitigations: 1) route non-latency-critical requests to smaller-quantized variants; 2) bring up a temporary fallback pool (V100/8x) and migrate queued jobs.

maya: Running quick triage commands now.
```bash
# show hpa / autoscaler status
kubectl get hpa -n infer prod-infer-hpa -o yaml
kubectl logs deployment/autoscaler -n kube-system --since=10m | tail -n 200
```

maya: autoscaler logs snippet:
```text
2026-03-14T02:09:54Z autoscaler ERROR: failed to provision nodes: RateLimitExceeded: Quota exceeded for CreateInstances
2026-03-14T02:10:01Z autoscaler WARN: backoff increased to 64s
2026-03-14T02:11:12Z autoscaler ERROR: all attempts failed, enqueueing scale request
```

lin: I just opened a cloud support case (#CLD-12345) requesting immediate quota bump and temporary removal of rate limits for our region. Support response ETA ~2 hours. Also checking if we can request emergency quota via partner channel.

oliver: Customer impact assessment: free-tier and standard customers see elevated latency / 429s. Premium/dedicated customers on Redwood Dedicated unaffected. I flagged top 5 paying customers to CS.

tee: Noted, pinged CS on escalation. We have two customers reporting production errors via support - IDs: C-4021, C-4027. Ryan, can you correlate logs and send quick status to them?

ryan: On it. Sending an interim message to affected customers: "We are experiencing elevated latencies due to autoscaler capacity issues; our SREs are actively mitigating. We'll update within 30 mins."

jess: Implementing fallback pool now. Command:
```bash
./tools/provision_fallback_pool --cluster prod --pool fallback-v100 --count 8 --gpu-type v100
kubectl annotate deployment infer-rt routing=drain-test
```

jess: Also enabling routing policy to divert low-priority traffic: set route weight general=0.1, premium=1.0.

maya: Applying throttling on api-gateway to protect cluster (temp):
```yaml
# ratelimit change
route: /v1/generate
limit: 10rps # global
exceptions:
  - customer_tier: premium
    limit: 100rps
```

alex: After throttle + fallback pool provisioning we see queue length start to drop from 12.4k -> 6.1k in ~7 minutes. Instance provisioning logs show some successful creates (4 nodes), but autoscaler still hitting intermittent 429s.

lin: Cloud support replied: they escalated our case, provisional capacity can be granted but still needs org approval ~45-90 minutes. They suggested staggering requests to reduce 429s.

jess: Quick change: reduce autoscaler parallelism and increase request interval to avoid API throttling. Patch applied to autoscaler config: parallelism=4 -> 2, request_interval=5s -> 8s.

maya: Observability note: created temporary dashboard with queue, scale_attempts, 429_rate. Alert thresholds adjusted to trigger at 2000 queued requests for paging.

alex: FYI — found a related bug where autoscaler retries weren't honoring exponential backoff properly causing storming behavior; logged as ENG-7891.

maya: Current state (02:42): queue ~3.8k, avg wait ~18s, fallback pool online (8 V100s), critical customer traffic routed correctly. No new customer 500s after throttle/wiring change.

oliver: Preparing customer-facing post: "We experienced elevated latencies due to autoscaler rate limits when provisioning GPU capacity. We routed traffic to fallback pools and throttled non-critical requests. We're working on long-term fixes."

maya: Handoff to next oncall (chen) at 03:15 UTC. Open items to track: 1) verify cloud quota increase (lin), 2) root cause for autoscaler burst retries + fix (alex/jess), 3) propagate routing and throttling playbook to runbook (maya/jess), 4) customer comms follow-up (oliver/tee).

chen: Taking over. Thanks @maya for the summary. I'll keep monitoring for 2 more hours then coordinate postmortem. Notes so far copied to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1765002468 (ops doc).

maya: Handing off checklist pasted here:
- Current mitigations: fallback pool (8 V100), global throttle (10rps default), premium exceptions in place.
- Observability: temp dashboard & alert lowered to 2k queued.
- Ongoing actions: cloud quota case #CLD-12345, ENG-7891 for autoscaler retry bug.
- Customer comms: interim message sent, CS ticket IDs C-4021,C-4027.

chen: Acknowledged. I'll update the incident doc with timeline + attach logs. I'll also schedule a 1hr post-incident review at 09:00 local.

ryan: Follow-up sent to customers with ETA and mitigation details. No escalation to legal/compliance required at this stage.

jess: Quick note — to avoid this class of issue we should: 1) add staggered provisioning in autoscaler, 2) implement a quota-aware scaler mode, 3) pre-warm minimal fallback pool for sudden spikes. Putting proposals in ENG board.

alex: Action items (short):
- ENG-7891: Fix autoscaler retry/backoff logic (owner: alex) — due 1 week.
- ENG-7892: Autoscaler config defaults: reduce parallelism, add quota-aware mode (owner: jess) — due 2 weeks.
- OPS-456: Add capacity rehearsal runbook + weekly run (owner: maya) — due 3 weeks.
- INFRA-321: Engage cloud partner for quota escalation and permanent increase (owner: lin) — due 48 hours.

maya: Quick retrospective note: The sudden spike coincided with a downstream client test that generated a large fan-out. Need better rate-limiting per-client. Adding runtime mitigations to prevent single-tenant storms.

tee: Thanks team — CS will prepare a concise customer postmortem once we have root cause.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: labels=[gpu_capacity, autoscaler, mitigation-fallback, customer-impact]. Severity set to Sev2. Incident owner: chen.

chen: Closing the live thread; I'll convert this to a formal postmortem doc and assign the tickets. If anything regresses ping me @chen. :thumbsup:"
